owner: Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop (page, posting as Jean Furlong)

items.author: moira.blyth
items.title: Light Up a Life details
items.body: Jean, here's everything for the tree post, hope it's all there. Memory tags in the shop from Monday 16 November, suggested donation £3, envelopes on the counter if people would rather write at home. Tree goes in the window on the Saturday and we switch the lights on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing, three or four carols, and Doreen is doing mince pies again. All the names on the tags get read out at the hospice remembrance service, Sunday 13 December, 3pm, in the day centre. People don't have to come to the service for their name to be read. Last year was 412 tags and £1,870, which Sandra says paid for most of a month of the night sitter service. Let me see it before it goes up? Thanks love. Moira

items.author: Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop
items.title: Light Up a Life 2025
items.body: Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the window again this year. Memory tags are on the counter from today, suggested donation £3. Lights on Saturday 29 November at 4pm. Every name will be read at the remembrance service on 14 December. Thank you, as always, for remembering with us. Jean

items.author: Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop
items.body: What an evening. Thank you to everyone who squeezed into Magdalen Street on Saturday, to the Gildencroft children for singing so beautifully in the cold, and to Doreen, whose mince pies did not survive the first carol. The tree now carries 412 names. We'll keep it lit until Twelfth Night.

items.author: Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop
items.body: We've been sent a wonderful box of Norfolk local history this week, including two of the old Jarrold guides and a lovely run of parish magazines from Sprowston. All priced and on the shelves by the door. Do come and have a rummage.

items.author: Hilary Gotts
items.body: Are you doing the tree again this year? Mum's name went on it last year and it meant the world. I'd like to bring my sister this time.

items.author: peter.danning
items.title: Rota
items.body: Morning Jean, any chance you could swap your Thursday the 19th for my Tuesday the 24th? Grandson's nativity. No worries if not. Peter

items.author: moira.blyth
items.title: Between us
items.body: Jean, strictly between us for now. The trustees met on Thursday and the Magdalen Street lease is under review. Rent is going up to £22,500 from April and there's talk of folding us into the Pottergate shop. Nothing decided, and they don't want a word of it out before the Christmas appeal, so please don't say anything on the page or to the other volunteers. I just didn't want you to hear it second-hand. M

items.author: Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop
items.body: A gentle reminder that we can't take encyclopaedias, Reader's Digest condensed books or anything that has been in a damp garage. Everything else, gratefully received Tuesday to Saturday, 10 till 4.

items.author: Jean Furlong
items.title: jottings for tree post
items.body: Seven years since Ray. First year I hung his tag I could barely write it. Now I write it in the shop at the counter, same pen. Want people to know they can just come and stand by the tree, no need to buy anything.

items.author: Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop
items.body: Christmas cards are in! Packs of ten for £4.50, designed by patients and families at the day centre. Every penny goes to hospice care at home.
